title: Jerusalem, 1099
hookLine: the First Crusade takes Jerusalem with great slaughter
last: THE SCHOOL OF MEDINA TRAVELED WEST.

cards: A group of refugees reaches Baghdad in the month of Ramadan. They have come a long way, from Syria and from Jerusalem. A judge brings them into the caliph's court, and they tell what they saw.
The chronicler Ibn al-Athir says their story brought tears to the eyes of those who heard it. Then he adds a line about the rulers: they were divided among themselves, and nothing was done.
This part of the path turns to the Crusades, the Mongols and the Mamluks, and it starts with the city those refugees had fled: Jerusalem.

teach.b: Jerusalem matters in Islam because of a journey. The Qur'an opens one of its surahs with it.
In Pickthall's translation: "Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed."
Muslims understand the Far Distant Place of Worship, al-Masjid al-Aqsa, to be in Jerusalem, and tradition says believers once faced toward it in prayer, before the Ka'bah.

teach.h: HOLY GROUND, SHARED IN MANY WAYS.
teach.b: So it was holy ground, shared in different ways with Jews and Christians, who hold it holy too. Armies from western Europe, the Franks of the First Crusade, marched a long way to take it.

teach.h: THE CITY FALLS, THE KILLING BEGINS.
teach.b: When the city fell, they killed a great many of the people inside. Muslim chroniclers like Ibn al-Athir describe killing in the Aqsa mosque itself, among scholars and devout people who had come to live near it.

A chronicler of Damascus, Ibn al-Qalanisi, writes that Jews were burned in their synagogue. Chroniclers among the Franks recorded the killing too. Nobody's numbers can be trusted, so i won't give any.
The Qur'an gives words for a moment of loss like this.

teach.h: WE ARE ALLAH'S, AND UNTO HIM RETURNING.
teach.b: In Pickthall's translation: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." Those words are still said at news of a loss.
Jerusalem, for a long time after, was a city in grief. And the refugees in Baghdad had named the problem the next generations would have to answer: a divided people.

how: Muslims say "inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" (we are God's, and to Him we return) at news of a death or loss, and al-Aqsa in Jerusalem is honored as the place of the Night Journey.

o: the city of the Night Journey, holy to three faiths
the city of the Ka'bah, where pilgrims make the hajj
the caliph's city, where the refugees told their story

p: the Far Distant Place of Worship
tells of the refugees in Baghdad
words for the moment of loss

s: only Muslims were killed when the city fell
Ibn al-Qalanisi writes that Jews were burned in their synagogue, and others died too.
tradition says believers once faced Jerusalem in prayer, before the Ka'bah
it was holy ground long before this day.
the rulers in Baghdad answered the refugees with an army at once
Ibn al-Athir says the court wept, but the rulers were divided and nothing was done.

games.q: you're a refugee from Jerusalem who has reached Baghdad in Ramadan. a judge offers to bring you before the caliph's court. what do you do?
o: stay silent and try to start a new life.
go in and tell them what you saw.
games.why: in Ibn al-Athir's account the refugees spoke and their hearers wept. but the rulers were divided, and nothing was done.

practice: Bring to mind the city that day, Muslims in the mosque, Jews in their synagogue, people of every faith in the streets, soldiers on every side; you don't need faces or numbers, just hold them all as people.

If you pray, you can pray for all who died there with the words the Qur'an gives for loss: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we are God's, and to Him we return. If you don't pray, simply keep a silence for them.

wordCard.voice: Jerusalem. The city of the Night Journey and the Aqsa mosque, holy to Muslims, Jews and Christians, and the city taken with great slaughter in the First Crusade. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the holy; the Arabic name for Jerusalem.

carryVoice: Your line: a city in grief. Behind every count were people with names. See you tomorrow.
